inputs.name: kappa
inputs.cite: PR-1 (paul@L43): 'around one mutation per 50 million bases'

inputs.name: L
inputs.cite: review reading of PR-1 'A few billion base pairs' (D/L does not depend on L)

day.reading: the model has no drift, so nothing fixes: D(t) counts differences between two individuals of one population, not fixed differences between species, and its zero transit time assumes the full-pipeline start Day disputes (M-202)
day.holds: the within-population prediction, 1.2% at 6.05 My, is about 14x measured human pairwise diversity (0.088%), so the model as a model of one population is falsified, as Paul concedes

critic.reading: read the two aliens as two isolated lineages with no ancestral polymorphism: the early limit 2 L kappa t is the neutral 2 mu T of B4a with theta_anc = 0, and k = mu (B5, M-209)
critic.holds: at Day's 3.0 inputs the neutral rate gives 1.512e7 substitutions per lineage against F_max 190.62, a factor of about 79,300; mutation supply (120 per generation) is not limiting against 1 fixation per 1,322 generations

notes: Every number in the EVOA-102 review's section 2 for the human-like model reproduces from Paul's inputs; the algebra is exact for n = 1..5. The review's '6.05 My (302,426 generations)' is the first generation at which D/L reaches 1.2%. E2: 1.2% against 0.088% is 13.6x (12x against the rounded 0.1%). Section 5: 1.512e7 / 190.62 = 79,320, stated 'about 79,000'. Whether D(t) speaks to fixed differences is the model question (E1, E3), not settled by this arithmetic.
